newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says weak mark bolstered 1996 earnings.
newsitem.headline: VW says weak mark bolstered 1996 earnings.

text.p: Volkswagen AG said on Thursday its 1996 earnings got a boost of about 600 million marks ($348.3 million) from the mark's weakening due to foreign currency market turbulence, and expected 1997 profits to also benefit.

VW chief financial officer Bruno Adelt said in the text of a speech at the German carmaker's annual news conference that the "favourable development" of the dollar, lira and pound last year compared to 1995 had led to the contribution to earnings.
"We did not expect the mark to weaken as much as it did last year," Adelt said in the speech, noting the rise of the dollar, lira and pound against the mark in the fourth quarter.
Adelt said VW's decision to retain some of the profits from 1996 would help 1997's results, which he said would also again likely benefit from VW's conservative stance on forex hedging.
